newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Friday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Friday:

Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Commission President Jacques Santer had stated that he shared the opinion of the Advisory Committee for Biotechnology Ethics that reproductive human cloning should be rejected. He said Santer had asked the services to examine the possibility to have it forbidden at Community level.

Spokeswoman Lousewies van der Laan briefed on Monday and Tueday's General Affairs Council. She said the ministers would notably have a general discussion on the situation in Ex-Yugoslavia before the end of EU special envoy Carl Bildt's mission. She said they would possibly discuss Bildt's successor.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the trade discussions at the General Affairs Council would focus on the EU/U.S. summmit results, preparation of the June 25 EU-Japan summit, leghold traps agreement, and draft strategy on EU-Hong Kong relations after 1997.

Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the ministers would also discuss the situation in the new Democratic Republic of Congo. He said the Commission would keep a prudent and coherent attitude. "In the framework of the humanitarian aid to the country it is clear for Commissioner de Deus Pinheiro that the EU cannot do less now than it did under Mobutu's regime," Vale de Almeida said.
In answer to a question Guilford said the Mutual Recognition Agreement had made substantial progress but was not concluded yet.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/451: Hindrances to Spanish fruit and vegetables.
- IP/97/458: Commission proposes technical specifications of euro coins.
- IP/97/463: World No-Tobacco Day, 31 May 1997: Statement by Commissioner Padraig Flynn.
- IP/97/464: MEDA-ECU 31 million for projects in Syria.
- Memo/97/55: Commission Calendar for the week of June 2-8, 1997.
- European Economy - Supplement A - Economic trends No 2: The legal framework of the euro.
